findings.title: Adapter settings, which may hold credentials, are written to adapter-config.json with default file permissions
findings.impact: The setup collects free-form adapter settings, such as `key = value` lines or a settings file. These commonly include API keys or tokens. The change writes them in plaintext to `<cwd>/triview-setup/adapter-config.json` using `writeFile` with default mode, usually 0644 under a typical umask. Other local users can read the file. It also sits inside the project directory, so it is easy to commit by accident. The setup output gives no warning. This adds a new on-disk copy of the secrets; the existing `routes.json` write has the same weakness.
findings.recommendation: Write the file with mode 0o600 (`writeFile(path, data, { mode: 0o600 })`) and create the directory with mode 0o700. Warn the user that the file may contain secrets. Consider adding the output directory to `.gitignore`, or let the config reference environment variables instead of storing secret values. Apply the same restrictive permissions to `routes.json`.
